name: DEEP CURRENT: Historical Lives Engine
description: A corponation-produced full-immersion sim published by Stratum Entertainment that allows players to inhabit reconstructed historical lives — not famous figures, but ordinary people: a fisherwoman on the Mekong Delta in 2031, a subway worker in Lagos during the Expansion Riots, a Bolivian alpaca herder watching the first orbital habitats rise. Each life runs 8-12 real hours and is built from archival neural-mapping research, oral histories, and environmental reconstruction. The sim is used in Meridian's Tier 3-4 educational institutions as accredited history curriculum.
story_hooks: An archivist discovers that one of DEEP CURRENT's 'reconstructed' historical lives is actually a real person who is still alive — and they never consented to having their neural architecture mapped.
A leaked DEEP CURRENT life — one that was never released — contains an ordinary person's memories of witnessing something a corponation desperately wants buried.

A Tier 1 kid pirating DEEP CURRENT lives becomes obsessed with a 2019 Lagos subway worker, convinced they're somehow a reincarnation — and the obsession is starting to affect their behavior in dangerous ways.
